one_line: The record-time writer is real and worth keeping, but as written there is no k-of-n trigger: "existed at the watermark" can't be rebuilt from the lookup row, the cause classifier sorts prose misses into the wrong class, D16 fires at k≥3 with no minimum n or window, and the trigger is expected to fire about never before KS-9 (E[k] about 0.001–0.05 per window); the dense carve-out recovers misses only as candidates, which still need a runnable check.

attacks.attack: 1. Replaying a lookup 'at the index watermark': can the watermark state (event set, recipe version, thresholds) be rebuilt from what §3.6 keeps, or does the replay run against today's index and over-count entries recorded after the miss?
attacks.evidence: Design line 290 (§3.6): the lookup row keeps the canonical query, handles, internal top-20 with features, what was shown, which thresholds fired, the gate verdict, the outcome, tokens, model, tier and wall time. It has no journal digest, no store-repo HEAD, no entry roster and no ingest high-water mark. Line 247: event provenance carries recipe_version and scrub_ruleset_sha, but not runner_version or the schema. Line 288: events carry only a per-entry Lamport counter, with no timestamp and no global order. Line 226: lookups are host-local, never journaled, and excluded from restore. Line 224: the index is a different file for each (schema, recipe, runner, scrub) tuple and is rebuilt from the journal. Line 361: §5.6's as-of fold needs a journal commit sha, which the lookup row does not record. Measured on this box (node 24.22.1, SQLite 3.53.4): an FTS5 MATCH whose terms share nothing with the row returns 0 rows ({ c: 0 }). So the stored top-20 is empty for exactly the vocabulary class. With §3.6's data, 'existed at the lookup's index watermark' can mechanically mean only one of three things: (a) the entry appears in the stored top-20 (empty for a vocabulary miss); (b) a wall-clock guess comparing the local-log file's mtime with the journal commit time (contrary to the design's events-not-time rule, and the mtime is lost on copy); (c) today's index. Option (c) counts an entry recorded after the miss by a parallel session. That case is the vocabulary case itself: claim signatures key on the wording (§7.5), so two sessions that word the same cause differently never collide. If the recipe changes between lookup and record, the class is computed across recipes, because the row keeps the canonical query, not the scrubbed raw text.
attacks.consequence: The lookup row must record what defines 'existed': the sorted live entry ids with their folded status at query time (an entry roster, at most about 200 ids, in the local log only), the store-repo HEAD sha, meta's journal digest, the full tool-version tuple, the θ values in force, and the scrubbed raw query so the class can be recomputed under a later recipe. 'Existed' = in the roster with a candidate-capable status. A lookup without a roster is 'unknown', never counted.

attacks.attack: 2a. Do the detectors share BM25's blind spot (Jaccard), and does hindsight wording in the draft fabricate 'same'?
attacks.evidence: Design line 453 (§7.3): the Jaccard near-duplicate check and the 'draft's own handles run as a lookup' both compare the draft, written after the solve, against existing entries. Neither compares the missed query. The draft's cause, diagnosis and ident handles (taken from the fix diff) describe the root cause in the same technical vocabulary as the existing entry's cause. So these two detectors are not blind the way the missed query was. Hindsight raises the detectors' recall. It does not decide the ruling or the cause class, which line 714 computes between the missed query and the existing entry.
attacks.consequence: none for detection. Hindsight's effect on k comes through 2b.

attacks.attack: 2b. Is a 'same' ruling an artefact of knowing the answer that inflates k? Count how many seed footprints share a file through the fix-diff join.
attacks.evidence: The fix-diff file sets of the mainline fix commits (git diff --name-only <c>^ <c>) are: ex1 2fe77f5, 13 files; ex6 1c546a3, 7; ex4 and ex5 together in one squash da988e2 (#170), 22 files; ex7 79a8dd4, 3; ex8 6928828, 4. Under §3.5's fix_diff tier, ex4 and ex5 therefore share all 22 files, including jobs/service.py, main.py, CLAUDE.md, HANDOFF and the mobile wizard files. ex1 and ex4/ex5 share customer_messaging/service.py and test_messaging_integration.py. Of the 45 non-seed fix commits on main, 23 (51%) touch at least one seed footprint file (fix_diff tier, plus ex3's AppContext.jsx/JobDetail.jsx and ex2a's versions directory), and 3 touch two or more. The hits come from jobs/service.py ×8, JobDetailScreen.tsx ×5, ArrivalJobWizard.tsx ×3, main.py ×2 and CLAUDE.md ×2. So the join gathers a seed entry for about half of all solves. It is also empty for fixes with no code diff: operator actions and deploy retries, the class §9 line 521 says is reachable only by wording. The inflation route is a mismatch between the ruling and the classifier. The ruling compares causes, and both causes are known after the solve. The classifier compares the missed query's words with the entry. A same-cause, different-symptom repeat with zero overlap therefore counts as 'vocabulary'. That is KS-C10's dominant repeat class ('share a root cause but land in a different file', refute-KS-C10-repo). A different symptom is not a paraphrase, so embeddings would not recover it either. 'same', 'related' and 'new' are defined nowhere (lines 453, 457), while §8 rule 1 makes ex1's Python and Node siblings share one root_cause row.
attacks.consequence: Define the rulings. same = the entry's symptom and cause cover the solved case, and the missed query is a description of the entry's symptom. related = same root_cause_id or same fix, but a different symptom. new = otherwise. Only a vocabulary-class 'same' counts toward D16. 'related' with zero overlap gets its own class (symptom_differs), which does not count. The join detector is acknowledged as low-precision recall and stays path-level.

attacks.attack: 3. The Opus ruling is an LLM relevance judgement (M-02 30: similarity scores and LLM judges ranked harmful memories no better than chance). What in the text bounds it: the reviewer re-check, a second ruling, a fixture?
attacks.evidence: Line 453 (§7.3) bounds only the consequence: 'acceptable here because it measures and opens an owner decision, never gates'. Line 457 (§7.4): the PR's Opus reviewer 're-checks every same / related / new ruling the author made'. It reads the author's ruling first, so it can anchor on it; it is the same model family; and it is the one review that is already mandatory. There is no second blind ruling and no labelled fixture. KS-2's done-when (line 583) tests only plumbing: 'a same ruling at record --lookup lands a missed_existing outcome with a cause class'. sweep/lane-M-02.md M02-30 is the register's own reason why the gate must be external and executable. Here, k (an LLM count) is what D16 hands the owner as evidence.
attacks.consequence: In §7.4, the reviewer rules blind before reading the author's ruling. A disagreement is recorded as disputed and not counted. A small fixture of labelled pairs from the seed is re-run whenever the ruling prompt changes: ex1's Python and Node siblings = related, ex7 vs ex8 = new, a paraphrase of ex3's toast = same. When D16 opens, the k items are listed verbatim (missed query beside the entry's title) for Fable and the owner to re-rule. k ≤ 10 is readable.

attacks.attack: 4. The lower bound and the denominator: can k ≥ 3 be reached on n = 3, and does 'k of n' as written stop a tiny-n install or a long-run ratchet?
attacks.evidence: D16 (line 714): the decision 'opens when k ≥ 3 vocabulary-class misses have been recorded … reported as k of n'. n is only reported. There is no minimum n and no window, so k=3 of n=3 and k=3 of n=300 both open it. §4.5 (line 325) makes n 'examined misses'. The v1.2 rule it claims to equal was 'at least ~5% of lookups over a sliding window of ~50' (sweep/lane-E-07.md line 43), with a lookup denominator and a window. So 'numerically the same as v1.2's 5% of 50' compares counts over different denominators and drops the window. The critic's point (4), that '3 ever' with no denominator ratchets (verdicts.txt line 147), was adopted as reporting only. Computed with exact binomial arithmetic (scratch rates.mjs), one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bounds: k=3/n=3 0.368; 3/10 0.087; 3/20 0.042; 3/50 0.017; 3/300 0.003. k=3 rejects a 5% vocabulary-miss share only for n ≤ 16, and a 10% share only for n ≤ 8.
attacks.consequence: D16 should read: the decision opens within one checkpoint window when k ≥ 3 vocabulary-class 'same' misses exist AND the exact one-sided binomial test rejects p ≤ 5% at 95%, over a denominator of examined lookups whose answer existed in the roster (hits on the right entry plus every missed_existing). For p0 = 5%, k = 3 qualifies only with n ≤ 16. Counts do not carry across windows. n, the unknown span and 'unexamined' are printed beside k. Strike 'numerically the same as v1.2's 5% of 50'.

attacks.attack: 5. Cause pre-classification by term overlap: can the vocabulary class be an artefact of the recipe or the FTS5 tokenizer (placeholders, masked numbers, stop words, stems)? Is edit distance ≤ 2 computed on terms or on the query?
attacks.evidence: Measured with node:sqlite FTS5 tokenize='porter unicode61' plus fts5vocab (scratch terms.mjs). FTS5 has no stop list. A real vocabulary-mismatch paraphrase ('customer was billed twice after the save button was pressed again on a slow connection') shares 'a', 'after' and 'the' with a synthetic ex3-style entry. That is not 'zero shared terms', so the rule classes it 'threshold', not 'vocabulary'. Only with the function words dropped is the shared set []. Recipe placeholders become ordinary terms: '<NUM>' and '{num}' → 'num', '<PATH>' → 'path', '<UUID>' → 'uuid'. Masking '429' in the query removes a term the entry's unmasked prose holds, and masking both sides creates a spurious shared 'num'. Edit distance on terms is not discriminating. Inside the one entry, 'bill'→'call' (2), 'slow'→'row' (2) and 'wa'→'a' (1). Against CLAUDE.md's 1,095 stems (433 of them ≤ 4 characters), 12 of 13 mismatch probe stems not in that vocabulary lie within distance 2 of some stem: twice→price, taken→token, lost→cost, spin→pin, slow→flow. The design does not say whether the distance is per term or per query (lines 325, 894). The four classes are not mutually exclusive and have no precedence. They are also not exhaustive: a miss caused by the status, existence, contradiction or not_when filters, or by the one-candidate display cap, fits none. A lookup that showed the wrong candidate is not a lookup.miss at all (line 333), so it falls outside the view.
attacks.consequence: Define the classifier in §4.5. Compute overlap over content terms: the canonical query and the entry's prose-table text tokenised with the index's own tokenizer, minus a fixed stop list and the recipe's placeholder tokens, IDF-weighted. typo = a query term of length ≥ 5 absent from the vocabulary, whose nearest term is within Damerau-Levenshtein 1 (2 at length ≥ 8), and whose substitution lifts coverage to θ_cand. Precedence: filtered → handle_gap → typo → vocabulary → threshold. Add 'filtered' and 'symptom_differs' classes. Golden fixtures for each artefact above go in KS-2's done-when.

attacks.attack: 6. The dense-only carve-out against KS-F11 and §4.1 step 4: what stops a dense neighbour surfacing an entry refuted at this footprint, fixed_off_main, superseded or capped? Is the status filter applied before or after the vector rank? Does a prose-only entry with no check dead-end?
attacks.evidence: §4.4 (line 321) puts the vectors in ranking ('fused by RRF for ranking') and adds the carve-out to abstention. It does not say that §4.1 step 2's status, existence and contradiction filters (line 301) apply to the KNN set before 'rank-1' and the margin are taken. 'Rank margin' is undefined (a rank gap is always 1) and is not among the θ values frozen at KS-4 (line 308). The fixed_off_main, provisional and contradiction caps are no-ops for a dense-only hit, which is already capped at candidate. not_when is matched lexically 'like tmpl/prose' (line 263), so it cannot fire on a zero-overlap query. Each new paraphrase re-surfaces the same refuted-by-wording entry, and the proposed_not_when built from 'the query handles the entry lacks' (line 313) can never converge. Only refuted-at-footprint suppression (keyed on the digest, not wording) would hold, and only if the status filter runs on the dense path. Dead ends: 'Only applies lets ks show print the fix' (line 304). A rule_without_case entry has 'no gate' (§8 rule 2, line 499), and the code-behaviour entries where silent and prose vocabulary misses occur (ex3, ex4, ex6) are unverified_seed or candidate-only until KS-6b (line 280). Under go-minimal, KS-6 is skipped (line 616). A recovered dense candidate on those entries ends at inconclusive and escalates as before.
attacks.consequence: In §4.4, the dense KNN runs over the step-2-filtered set; the margin is a cosine-similarity gap calibrated by leave-one-handle-out with out-of-corpus abstention; any not_when is also matched by dense similarity, or else a dense-only candidate on an entry with an active not_when is suppressed. A dense-only hit on an entry with no runnable check prints a one-line pointer (no card) and is counted as dense_dead_end. The claim narrows to: the carve-out turns a zero-overlap miss into a shown candidate. Recovery past the gate exists only for entries with a runnable check.

attacks.attack: 7. RT-06: can v_missed_existing, its k and n, or 'unexamined' read zero for a reason other than 'no misses'? List each path and whether 'unexamined' covers it.
attacks.evidence: Paths: (a) An escalation with no lookup leaves no lookup row; 'unexamined' is computed from lookup rows (line 325), so it does not cover this (self-reported only, §7.8). (b) Exit 3 or 4 (line 431): no lookup id is printed, so the record cannot name one; not covered. (c) A rephrase that hits: miss A, then lookup B leads to X, applies, resolved. That is reuse, not a §7.3 hard solve (line 451), so there is no record. A stays 'unexamined' forever and never enters k, although it is the cleanest vocabulary signal. Covered as unexamined only. (d) A tool-version bump: line 224 opens a new index file rebuilt 'from the journal'. KS-1's rebuild (line 570) ingests the journal only, and lookups live in store/local/ (line 226). Unless the local log is re-ingested, both the lookup.miss join (line 333) and 'unexamined' read 0. Not covered. (e) A restore or another host: 'A restore therefore excludes lookups by design' (line 226). The missed_existing outcome events are journaled, but the view requires the lookup.miss row, so k reads 0 too. The rollups carry counts (line 226), but the views do not fall back to them. Not covered. (f) All three detectors find nothing: a vocabulary miss on an operator-action or trap entry with no code fix diff (2b), where two detectors are wording-based. The miss counts in n as examined, k stays 0, and it is not 'unexamined'. Not covered. (g) A lookup that predates a later schema field (the roster proposed in attack 1) must read 'unknown'. (h) A shown-wrong candidate, with the right entry below the display cap, is not a lookup.miss. Excluded by definition.
attacks.consequence: In §3.1 and KS-1, rebuild and any new version-keyed index re-ingest store/local/. The rollup events carry k, n and unexamined, and after a restore the views sum the rollups. Each view reports 'unknown since <date>' when the local log does not span its window. §4.5 lists paths (a), (b) and (f) as known undercounts. Add a mechanical writer for (c) (see the rephrase-then-hit row).

attacks.attack: 8. Can KS-O18's 'k ≥ 3 vocabulary misses' fire in practice, given that §7.3 records only escalations, two or more failed approaches or burned builds, and given a pilot corpus of about 15 entries? Estimate the base rate from KS-C10's prior and say whether the trigger is decorative.
attacks.evidence: Main's active history is 2026-05-31 to 2026-08-03 (git log origin/main), with 50 fix-prefixed commits. KS-C10 found 3–5 same-cause repeats in that 65-day window. Under the KS-F17 counting rule, f29f62f (findable by git log --grep), 0a3b38e and 981ae08 drop out (refute-KS-C10-repo), leaving about 2 servable repeats, about 1.7 per 8-week KS-9 window. Multiply by P(the first occurrence is in the store; about 15 seed entries, lazy seeding thereafter) 0.3–0.5 × P(lookup ran) 0.6–0.9 × P(miss) 0.3–0.5 × P(zero shared terms) 0.05–0.2. The last factor is Chaparro et al., ICSME 2016, as researched in verdicts.txt line 336: 5.1% of duplicate pairs share no term on title plus description, 19% on description alone. Under the no-stop-list rule of attack 5 it is about 0. Then × P(record with --lookup) 0.5–0.7 × P(detected and ruled same) 0.6–0.9. That gives E[k] of 1.4e-3 to 4.9e-2 per window. Poisson P(k ≥ 3) is 1.9e-5 at the high end, 3.6e-3 even at λ = 0.3, and 0.58 only at λ = 3 (scratch rates.mjs). With D16 windowless (attack 4), the trigger is decorative within the pilot and KS-9 horizon and can fire only by piling up across the program, which is the ratchet the critique warned of.
attacks.consequence: In §11 D16 and §9, state that the trigger is not expected to fire before KS-9, so D16 is a later-program decision. The record-time check's value before then is the per-miss record: the missed wording becomes a proposed_handle, which fixes the specific miss with no install. Apply the windowed binomial rule (attack 4) so accumulation cannot substitute for evidence.

attacks.attack: 9 (added). A dense-only candidate on a necessary_condition entry bypasses KS-F8's cause-specific template requirement through the candidate route.
attacks.evidence: Line 277 (§3.4, KS-F8): 'a lead for a remote-resolver entry also needs the caller's raw symptom to match a cause-specific template'. That is scoped to a lead. Line 304: 'Only applies lets ks show print the fix'. Line 321: dense-only may raise 'to candidate, never to lead, still behind the gate'. Line 446 (§7.2): a candidate is verified, and on applies its fix is used. A dense-only hit has zero lexical overlap by construction, so it never matches the template. For ex7 (a necessary_condition data value), any Android-build-failure description lands nearest to ex7 or ex8 in a 15-entry vector space. A co-present empty env value then returns applies and the fix is printed: §9's latent co-present cause (line 517), now reachable from zero-overlap queries. ex8 stays safe only because its EAS-secret precondition is unprobed (inconclusive).
attacks.consequence: In §3.4 and §4.4, extend KS-F8's template requirement from leads to any candidate that reaches applies on a necessary_condition entry: without the template match, the verdict is inconclusive(symptom_unmatched) and the fix stays withheld. Add a KS-5 or ks eval probe: an unrelated Gradle failure paraphrase against ex7.

attacks.attack: 10 (added). Parallel sessions and git worktrees on old branches: whose index does the record-time replay use?
attacks.evidence: Line 224 keys an index file by tool-version tuple, and line 525 (§9) says a worktree on an old branch runs an old CLI that 'rebuilds its own index file'. A lookup made with the old CLI in a release/drain worktree and a record made with the new CLI therefore read different index files. The record cannot replay 'at the lookup's watermark' in the index that answered, and the lookup's internal top-20 features (line 290) were computed under the old recipe. With no roster (attack 1), the replay runs on the newest index and its current event set.
attacks.consequence: This is covered by the roster amendment: existence is decided by the roster stored in the lookup row, not by any index file. The cause class is recomputed from the stored scrubbed raw query under the current recipe, and both recipe versions are recorded on the outcome event.

attacks.attack: 11 (added). Are dense ranks and margins deterministic across Windows and the Linux VPS or CI (KS-F4's cross-platform top-k equality)?
attacks.evidence: KS-F4 (line 785) requires the top-k output of a tie fixture set to be equal on Windows and on the ubuntu CI job. §4.4 makes vectors a per-host derived column computed by transformers.js int8 bge-small. Nothing is installed (the no-install rule), so cross-host cosine values and margin decisions could not be compared. node:sqlite does expose loadExtension with allowExtension:true on this box (checked), so the sqlite-vec route itself is not blocked.
attacks.consequence: If D16 ever fires, extend KS-1's cross-platform tie fixture to the dense rank and the margin decision, and record the model id, revision and runtime per vector and per host.

counter_evidence:
1. The lookup row does not record what 'existed' needs. §3.6 (design line 290) keeps no journal digest, store HEAD, entry roster or ingest mark. Events have no timestamp (line 288). Lookups are host-local and excluded from restore (line 226). The index is a separate file per tool-version tuple (line 224). For the class that counts, the stored top-20 is empty: a zero-overlap FTS5 MATCH returns 0 rows, measured on node 24.22.1 with SQLite 3.53.4.

2. The cause classifier puts prose misses in the wrong class. Measured with FTS5 porter/unicode61, which has no stop list: a real paraphrase shares 'a', 'after' and 'the' with the entry, so the rule classes it 'threshold', not 'vocabulary'. Placeholders tokenise to 'num', 'path' and 'uuid'. A term-level edit distance of 2 or less links 12 of 13 mismatch stems to a CLAUDE.md stem. The four classes have no precedence and are not exhaustive.

3. D16 is not a k-of-n rule. It fires at k≥3 with no minimum n and no window (line 714). Its claimed equivalence to v1.2's '5% of a sliding 50-lookup window' (lane-E-07 line 43) swaps the denominator and drops the window. k=3 rejects a 5% vocabulary-miss share only when n is 16 or less.

4. The trigger is decorative before KS-9. Main had about 2 store-servable repeats in 65 days (KS-C10 under KS-F17). That gives an expected k of about 0.001–0.05 per KS-9 window and P(k≥3) of about 2e-5 at the high end. The trigger can fire only by accumulating across the program.

5. The detectors over-gather and miss non-code fixes. 23 of 45 non-seed main fix commits share a file with a seed fix-diff footprint, mostly through the 22-file #170 squash that bundles ex4 and ex5. The join detector is empty for fixes that have no code diff.

6. The ruling and the classifier measure different things. Same/related/new are undefined. The ruling compares causes while the classifier compares words, so same-cause, different-symptom repeats (KS-C10's dominant class) can count as 'vocabulary'.

7. The Opus ruling's accuracy is unchecked. Its only check is a non-blind reviewer re-check; there is no second ruling and no fixture.

8. Several paths make the views read zero for the wrong reason, and 'unexamined' does not cover them: a rebuild or a restore drops the local-log lookups that the view joins on, and k reads 0 even though the outcomes are journaled.

9. The dense carve-out's order against the status filters is unspecified. not_when cannot fire on a dense-only hit. Check-less and pre-KS-6b entries dead-end at the gate. A dense candidate on a necessary_condition entry can reach applies without the KS-F8 template that a lead needs.
narrowed_claim: `ks record --lookup` gives v_missed_existing a writer. For misses that end in a recorded hard solve, it names the missed entry and an Opus same/related/new ruling, and the record-time check is worth keeping because it turns the missed wording into a proposed_handle. It becomes a measurable trigger only after four changes. First, the lookup row stores an entry roster, journal HEAD, journal digest, tool versions, θ values and the scrubbed raw query, and 'existed' means 'in the roster'. Second, the classifier is defined over content terms with a stop list, placeholder exclusion, a strict typo rule, precedence and filtered/symptom_differs classes. Third, the rulings are defined and the reviewer re-checks blind against a fixture. Fourth, a mechanical writer covers rephrase-then-hit. Even then, D16 as written (k ≥ 3, no minimum n, no window) is not a k-of-n rule, and it is not expected to fire before KS-9 (E[k] about 0.001–0.05 per window). The dense-only carve-out does make a zero-overlap query reachable as a candidate. Past the gate, it recovers only entries with a runnable check, and only once its filter order, not_when handling and the KS-F8 template requirement are specified.
what_would_settle_it:
For the parts that stay unverifiable:
(1) The Opus ruling's false-'same' rate: a labelled fixture of seed pairs (ex1 Python/Node = related; ex7/ex8 = new; a paraphrase of ex3's toast = same) ruled blind by two Opus sessions at KS-2. Report agreement and accuracy.
(2) Whether `ks rebuild` re-ingests store/local/: a KS-1 test that bumps recipe_version and asserts that v_missed_existing, n and unexamined survive.
(3) Dense-only behaviour at seed scale: at KS-4 corpus size, run ks eval's out-of-corpus set through a pinned int8 bge-small (only if D16 fires). Report the dense-only candidate rate on queries that must abstain, and the margin distribution.
(4) Cross-host determinism: compute the same vectors on Windows and the ubuntu job and compare the margin decisions.
(5) The real base rate: the KS-9 prospective log's k, n and unexamined, with the unknown spans reported.

amendments.change: Add to the lookup row: entry_roster (sorted live entry ids with their folded status at query time; host-local log only), journal_head (store-repo HEAD sha), index_watermark (meta journal digest), the tool-version tuple (schema, recipe, runner, scrub), the θ/μ values in force, and the scrubbed raw query text. Define 'existed at the lookup's index watermark' as 'in entry_roster with a candidate-capable status'. A lookup without a roster is unknown and never counted.
amendments.why: With what §3.6 keeps, the watermark cannot be rebuilt: no digest, no HEAD, no timestamps, and a top-20 that is empty for a zero-overlap miss. A replay against today's index counts entries recorded after the miss by parallel sessions, precisely in the vocabulary class.

amendments.change: `ks rebuild` and any new version-keyed index file re-ingest store/local/ lookups and gate runs. Rollup events carry k, n and unexamined for v_missed_existing. After a restore or on a host without the local log, the views sum the rollups and print 'unknown since <date>' for uncovered spans. Add a KS-1 test that bumps recipe_version and asserts the view and its counts survive.
amendments.why: The view joins lookup.miss rows, which live only in the host-local log. A rebuild from the journal or a restore makes k, n and unexamined read 0, which is RT-06's unknown-as-zero.

amendments.change: Define the classifier. Overlap is computed over content terms, with the canonical query and the entry's prose-table text tokenised by the index's own porter/unicode61 tokenizer, minus a fixed stop list and the recipe's placeholder tokens (num, uuid, hex, path, …), IDF-weighted. typo = a query term of length ≥ 5 absent from the vocabulary, whose nearest vocabulary term is within Damerau-Levenshtein 1 (2 at length ≥ 8), and whose substitution lifts coverage to θ_cand. Precedence: filtered → handle_gap → typo → vocabulary → threshold. Add 'filtered' (status, existence, contradiction, not_when or display-cap misses) and 'symptom_differs' (a related ruling with zero overlap). State that shown-wrong candidate lookups are outside the view. Golden fixtures for function words, placeholders and short-stem distance go in KS-2's done-when.
amendments.why: Measured: FTS5 keeps 'a/after/the', so a real paraphrase classes as threshold. Placeholders tokenise to shared terms. Term-level distance ≤ 2 links 12 of 13 mismatch stems to the CLAUDE.md vocabulary. The four classes overlap and are not exhaustive.

amendments.change: Define the rulings. same = the entry's symptom and cause cover the solved case and the missed query describes the entry's symptom. related = same root_cause_id or fix, different symptom. new = otherwise. Restrict the detectors to the lookup's roster. Add a mechanical writer: a miss followed, in the same actor_session or claim, by a lookup whose gate returns applies on entry X and whose outcome is resolved writes outcome(missed_existing, X, the missed lookup, class by term overlap, ruled_by: mechanical). Note that the fix-diff join is empty for fixes without a code diff.
amendments.why: Without definitions, same-cause, different-symptom repeats (KS-C10's dominant class) count as vocabulary misses that embeddings cannot recover. Rephrase-then-hit is the cleanest vocabulary signal, and it never reaches `ks record`.

amendments.change: The reviewer rules every same/related/new blind, before reading the author's ruling. A disagreement is recorded as disputed and not counted. A labelled fixture from the seed (ex1 Python/Node = related; ex7/ex8 = new; a paraphrase of ex3's toast = same) is re-run whenever the ruling prompt changes.
amendments.why: The only bound on the LLM relevance judgement (M-02 30) is a non-blind re-check by the same model family. KS-2's done-when tests only plumbing.

amendments.change: Replace 'opens when k ≥ 3' with: 'opens within one checkpoint window when k ≥ 3 vocabulary-class same misses AND the exact one-sided binomial test rejects a vocabulary-miss share ≤ 5% at 95%, over examined lookups whose answer was in the roster (hits on the right entry plus every missed_existing); for 5%, k = 3 qualifies only with n ≤ 16; counts do not carry across windows; k, n, unexamined and unknown spans are printed together; each counted item is listed verbatim for Fable and the owner to re-rule'. Strike 'numerically the same as v1.2's 5 % of 50'. Add: 'not expected to fire before KS-9 (E[k] about 0.001–0.05 per window from KS-C10's prior)'.
amendments.why: As written, n is only reported, so the rule opens at 3/3 and ratchets at 3/300. v1.2's rule had a lookup denominator and a 50-lookup sliding window (lane-E-07 line 43).

amendments.change: The dense KNN runs over the set already passed by §4.1 step 2's status, existence and contradiction filters. The margin is a cosine-similarity gap calibrated by leave-one-handle-out, with out-of-corpus abstention, and recalibrated with the θ values. A dense-only candidate on an entry with an active not_when is suppressed unless the not_when is also matched by dense similarity. A dense-only hit on an entry with no runnable check prints a one-line pointer and is counted as dense_dead_end. Vectors, model id, revision and runtime are stamped per host, and KS-F4's tie fixture extends to dense ranks.
amendments.why: The order is unspecified; not_when is lexical, so it can never fire on a dense-only hit; the caps are no-ops for it; and check-less or pre-KS-6b entries (ex3, ex4, ex6, rule_without_case) dead-end at the gate.

amendments.change: Extend the necessary_condition rule. Any candidate (dense-only included) that reaches applies on a necessary_condition entry without a cause-specific template match returns inconclusive(symptom_unmatched), with the fix withheld. Add a ks eval or KS-5 probe: an unrelated Gradle-failure paraphrase against ex7.
amendments.why: KS-F8's template requirement is scoped to leads, so the candidate route, widened by the dense carve-out to zero-overlap queries, reaches §9's latent co-present cause.

amendments.change: Add: v_missed_existing undercounts three things: escalations without a lookup, exit-3/4 lookups (no id), and vocabulary misses on fixes without a code diff where the wording-based detectors also miss. The D16 trigger is decorative within the pilot and KS-9 horizon. The record-time check's near-term value is the proposed_handle from the missed wording.
amendments.why: These are the zero-for-the-wrong-reason paths that 'unexamined' does not cover, plus the base-rate estimate.

amendments.change: KS-2 done-when adds: the roster on the lookup row; classifier fixtures (function words, placeholders, short-stem distance, precedence); the mechanical rephrase-then-hit writer; the blind-ruling fixture. KS-9 reports k, n, unexamined, the window, the unknown spans and the per-item list.
amendments.why: Gives the narrowed mechanism a test and a readable report.

could_not_run: Replaying a real lookup at its index watermark: the store, index and local log do not exist (no tools/ks).
The Opus same/related/new false-'same' rate: needs real record-time rulings or a labelled fixture run by Opus sessions.
Whether ks rebuild or a new version-keyed index re-ingests store/local/: no code exists, so the finding rests on the text (§3.1, KS-1 scope).
v_missed_existing, k, n and 'unexamined' on real data, and the KS-9 base rate: they need the prospective log.
Dense-only candidate rates on out-of-corpus queries and margin distributions at seed scale: no embedding model installed (no-install rule).
Cross-host determinism of transformers.js int8 bge-small vectors (Windows against Linux): no model and no Linux host here.
The base-rate estimate's multiplicative factors (compliance, miss rate, record rate) are assumptions bounded by KS-C10 and Chaparro et al.; only the KS-9 log measures them.
